item.title: LACMA Workers Vote Overwhelmingly to Unionize
item.description: A whopping 96% of staff at the Los Angeles County Museum of Art voted in favor of a union, calling for higher pay and “increased transparency.”

item.title: Debt Plagues Artists Regardless of Career Stage, Survey Finds
item.description: Data compiled by artist mentor Paddy Johnson from over 1,000 respondents indicates that “artists across all levels struggle with a lot of the same things.”

item.title: The Best Art Shows Around the World in 2025
item.description: Nan Goldin’s fearless photos, Noah Davis’s enchantments of ordinary life, Stan Douglas’s historical visions, and Yoko Ono’s musical mind were just some of our favorites.

item.title: Art Movements: New York City's 27-Foot Buddha
item.description: Tuan Andrew Nguyen tapped for High Line commission, PAIN's Megan Kapler heads to Housing Works, the Whitney Biennial, and more.

item.title: The World's Best Art in 2025
item.description: Also: A majority of artists struggle with debt, LACMA workers vote overwhelmingly for a union, and a word about the hilarity of evil.

item.title: How a Nativity Scene Sent Europe Into a Tizzy
item.description: A controversial Brussels nativity scene begs the question: Should explicitly Christian imagery continue to be a part of Europe’s civic space, and if so, who has the authority to define it?

item.title: Medieval Psalms Were Not For Everyone
item.description: An exhibition prioritizes the expensive, silent object over the lived, functional experience of the believer.

item.title: “Victims of Communism” Monument Altered Over Reported Nazi Ties
item.description: A memorial in Canada will no longer include the names of specific people after the government said it found possible Nazi affiliations among the commemorated individuals.

item.title: Trump-Appointed NEA Chair Returns for Second Term
item.description: Mary Anne Carter led the National Endowment for the Arts during Trump’s first presidency.

item.title: Dear Zohran, Don’t Let Art Workers Down
item.description: Those of us in the cultural sector need you to enact a bold vision for the role of city government in fostering the arts and helping our communities thrive.
